To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

early liver transplantation in patients with alcoholic hepatitis has excellent 1 year survival and is associated with low rates of alcohol recidivism, suggesting that the 6 month abstinence rule may not be required in all patients.

liver transplantation for severe alcohol hepatitis (SAH), in patients who are nonresponders to steroids, has excellent outcomes and is associated with similar rates of recidivism to patients with alcoholic cirrhotic liver disease who are sober for 6 months prior to liver transplantation.
early liver transplant for patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis (defined as a Lille score >0.45) results in similar outcomes as those patients who have 6 months of abstinence.
